title: Appeals and merit-system complaints, by kind, fiscal 2020-21 to 2024-25
question: What do employees, applicants and unions bring to the Civil Service Commission, and is it rising?
finding: Appeals and hearing requests before the Commission (new plus carried over) went from 95 in 2020-2021 to 116 in 2024-2025; in the last year 38 were about examinations, 39 about discrimination and 35 about bars on future City employment. Only 3 appeals in five years were about personal-services contracts. Inspection-service requests in the report’s chart went from 43 to 112; in 2024-2025 32 concerned certification and selection, 10 conflicts of interest and 7 appointments. The report lists the complaints as including favoritism, nepotism, appointees not meeting the minimum qualifications, order of layoff, probationary periods, reversion rights, out-of-class assignments, status grant, disqualification after appointment to the position, ….
how: Figures are the data behind the two charts embedded in the Commission’s five-year annual report (Word file), read as stored; the text of the report is quoted for the complaint topics. Counts are as the Commission reports them; appellants and complainants are never named or counted individually here.
limits: “Received” in the chart counts new appeals plus those carried over, so years overlap. An appeal or complaint is an allegation; most examination appeals are denied. The chart’s inspection counts differ slightly from the counts in the report’s text for some years.

sources.t: San Francisco Civil Service Commission: Annual Report, fiscal years 2020-2025 (transmitted 26 January 2026)
